checks.finding: Tfast/Tslow and operator_total_q are independent members. ensureProbabilities only lazily decays them; it separately resets and sums temporary probability totals. Extra accepted-event work O(1); probability queries retain O(K), no new KP scan.

New next ordinal is deduplicated before any refresh/share/count. Both persistent totals and selected fast/slow mass advance to common q. pf/ps use matching priors and counts excluding current label; rational posterior is log-loss eta1 update; alpha+(1-2alpha)posterior is sharing to OTHER expert.

Only accepted public next PROBE inserts mass; current miss refresh/observe/refault does not add expert sample. Legal callbacks have monotonic hit+miss and next=q+1. max(ordinal,total_q) prevents rewind; max query q includes last accepted next and total clock. Arbitrarily delayed labels supplied through private test entry are outside official callback semantics, not an official engine bug.

Query operator marginal is w*fast+(1-w)*slow. operator_scale divides by slow operator mass+64/K; unchanged ensureProbability supplies original adaptive slow conditional numerator. Joint sum is 1 up to roundoff under legal finite counts. No mixed probability feeds raw counts.

Accepted sample invalidates probability cache; release already invalidates before any proposal; epoch wrap is unchanged. Dimension reset clears both totals, clock, weight=.5 and probability cache. Duplicate removal of refresh is harmless for legal callbacks: miss refresh and query refresh retain lazy aging without a learning trial.

Added behavior uses public next and hit/miss counters and its own statistics only. Callback/action bodies, actual record, scan/cycle guards, partition refault base, H estimator, horizon64/proxy100 and official framework are unchanged. Positive K/P and valid IDs are inherited official legal-input assumptions.

Positive prior keeps legal prequential forecasts positive; finite/weight guards fall back to .5, clamp within alpha..1-alpha. This is not a general repair for corrupt/infinite state, nor bit identity with either endpoint. Prediction objective is on policy-selected observed next labels; no claim of IO/D improvement, unbiased full-access estimation or universal prior optimality.
